measurements_m.method: Three 28-rib profiles in the upper sail give median visible rib widths of 11–12% of the 0.3048 m pitch described in the 1914 plant report. Rounded display cross-section represents grouped ribs.

measurements_m.what: Highest sail above ground at the displayed orientation
measurements_m.method: Display pose, not a fixed historic clearance. The 102 ft spar at 35 degrees from vertical and 12 degrees of tilt, an estimated 19.55 m hub, and the outer lattice corner give about 33.6 m.

checkpoints.what: Highest sail at the displayed rotor angle

simplified: The mapped 18.25 × 18.32 m outline is the projecting gallery, used directly at 5.5 m. Its edge extends up to 4.19 m beyond the documented 10.06 m diameter ground footing. The ground plan follows that published physical foundation.
The cap faces the prevailing westerlies. The rotor is fixed at 35° from vertical; its upper sail rises above the measured cap. The open sails group the lattice into five broad bays per blade.
A 12° tilt gives the lower sails clearance outside the gallery. The bearing housing, sixteen grouped gallery posts and one continuous rail are shown.

The NPS north-mill photograph shows a rounded, continuously tapering shaft and circular gallery. The model uses a 32-sided cone with smooth normals. Individual sail lattice ribs are grouped and thickened.
